title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #14

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A melodic percussion instrument is one that (1 mark)
   A. has no parts
   B. can only make one sound
   C. is always loud
   D. can play different notes to make a tune

2. Which is a melodic percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Claves
   B. Kayamba
   C. Xylophone
   D. Cowbell

3. What is the job of the hollow shell of a drum? (1 mark)
   A. To make the sound fuller and louder
   B. To keep the skin wet
   C. To tie the ropes
   D. To hold the beater

4. Where must a player stand to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. Anywhere on the court
   B. At the centre circle
   C. Inside the goal circle
   D. Behind the goal post

5. What do the letters WA stand for? (1 mark)
   A. Winning Arm
   B. Water Aim
   C. Wing Ally
   D. Wing Attack

6. The first step of tying an overhand knot is to (1 mark)
   A. wet the cord
   B. burn the cord
   C. make a loop
   D. cut the cord

7. In a chest pass your thumbs turn downwards (1 mark)
   A. as you release the ball
   B. never
   C. when you sit
   D. before you catch

8. How many secondary colours are there on the basic colour wheel? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Nine
   C. Three
   D. Two

9. A lighter tone of a colour is called a (1 mark)
   A. shade
   B. tint
   C. outline
   D. primary

10. Where do you place a soft shadow when painting a fruit on a table? (1 mark)
   A. Nowhere
   B. On the ceiling
   C. Inside the fruit
   D. On the table under the fruit

11. Which colours are the primary colours? (1 mark)
   A. Red, yellow and blue
   B. Red, green and brown
   C. Black, white and grey
   D. Orange, green and purple

12. Which is the highest of the notes d, r and m? (1 mark)
   A. m
   B. They are all the same
   C. d
   D. r

13. The shield and two crossed spears on the flag stand for (1 mark)
   A. sports
   B. defence of freedom
   C. farming
   D. music

14. The bottom stripe of the Kenyan flag is (1 mark)
   A. red
   B. black
   C. white
   D. green

15. Which is part of a good warm-up? (1 mark)
   A. Sitting still
   B. Sleeping
   C. Eating a large meal
   D. Gentle jogging and stretching

16. Why do we warm up before sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. To tire out the muscles
   B. To hide from the starter
   C. To make the track smooth
   D. To prepare muscles and avoid injury

17. Where should your hands be at the start? (1 mark)
   A. Far in front of the line
   B. Over the line
   C. In your pockets
   D. Just behind the start line

18. On the Kenyan flag, red stands for (1 mark)
   A. the blood shed in the struggle for freedom
   B. the land
   C. peace
   D. the sky

19. In a side roll, your body should be (1 mark)
   A. bent at the waist
   B. curled like a ball
   C. hanging in the air
   D. straight and long like a log

20. In a crab balance, your body is supported by (1 mark)
   A. the head only
   B. the back only
   C. the knees and elbows
   D. both hands and both feet

21. How long should you hold a crab balance in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Half a second
   B. Ten minutes
   C. Three to five counts
   D. One hour

22. Dynamics means (1 mark)
   A. the speed
   B. how loud or soft the music is
   C. the words
   D. the pitch

23. Singing in unison means (1 mark)
   A. everyone sings different tunes
   B. only one sings
   C. everyone sings the same notes at the same time
   D. nobody sings

24. The element of light means (1 mark)
   A. how well the subject is lit
   B. the weight of the camera
   C. the price
   D. the size of the photo

25. Which light is best for outdoor photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Natural sunlight falling on the subject
   B. Darkness
   C. Only midday shadows
   D. A torch in the eyes

26. The flash is (1 mark)
   A. the button
   B. the strap
   C. the screen
   D. a small light for dark places

27. How many lines are on a staff? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Three
   C. Five
   D. Ten

28. Which hand is at the top of the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Left
   B. Neither
   C. Both feet
   D. Right

29. In a prone float, you keep your body (1 mark)
   A. curled with head up
   B. long and relaxed with face in the water
   C. stiff and bent
   D. standing

30. Which float has the body curled up like a ball? (1 mark)
   A. Supine float
   B. Prone float
   C. Mushroom float
   D. Glide

31. Which is part of pool hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Eating in the pool
   B. Wearing dirty clothes
   C. Not passing urine or spitting in the pool
   D. Not showering

32. If someone is drowning, the safest action for a child is to (1 mark)
   A. shout for an adult and throw something that floats
   B. run away silently
   C. laugh
   D. jump in to save them

33. A swimming cap is useful for (1 mark)
   A. drying
   B. making you float
   C. keeping long hair out of the way
   D. holding a whistle

34. Supine means (1 mark)
   A. face down
   B. curled
   C. standing
   D. face up

35. Monkey swing helps to develop (1 mark)
   A. balance and coordination
   B. only hearing
   C. only counting
   D. only reading

36. Which game builds strong arms and shoulders as you crawl on hands and toes? (1 mark)
   A. Snake slither
   B. Elephant walk
   C. Giraffe stretch
   D. Crocodile crawl

37. The hare hop is done (1 mark)
   A. by sitting
   B. by rolling
   C. by hopping forward with both feet like a hare
   D. by crawling

38. Which value is found in the Kenya National Anthem? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating
   B. Unity
   C. Laziness
   D. Selfishness

39. How should you care for displayed works? (1 mark)
   A. Touch to feel the paint
   B. Tear the corners
   C. Do not touch or write on them
   D. Leave them in the rain

40. Which is a focus when analysing a team sport performance? (1 mark)
   A. Teamwork and safety
   B. The weather only
   C. The price of the ball
   D. The colour of shoes only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three safety measures to observe when playing netball. (3 marks)

42. When is an overhead pass better than a chest pass? (2 marks)

43. Name the three secondary colours and state how each is made. (3 marks)

44. How can you show that you have identified the pitch of a note by ear? (3 marks)

45. Give three examples of good etiquette during a performance. (3 marks)

46. State four rules for playing the hawk and the chicks game. (4 marks)

47. Explain the difference between a sacred song and a patriotic song. (3 marks)

48. Explain how good singing performance is achieved, using posture, breathing, diction, expression and etiquette. (5 marks)

49. Name two animal movement games. (2 marks)

50. Explain what is meant by two stars and a wish in feedback. (3 marks)

51. What does it mean to improvise a rhythmic pattern? (3 marks)

52. What does giving with the ball mean in netball catching? (2 marks)

53. Why should the flag stick be held high while cheering? (2 marks)

54. Describe how to compose, write and perform an original four-beat rhythmic pattern. (5 marks)

55. What is a rest in music? (2 marks)

56. Describe how to draw a drum with tonal value using the smudge technique. (4 marks)

57. Describe how you would improvise a rhythm to accompany a song. (4 marks)

58. Describe how to do the frog jump. (3 marks)

59. Name the three primary colours. (2 marks)

60. State the three commands at the start of a sprint race in order. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — can play different notes to make a tune
   Melodic instruments such as the xylophone play notes of different pitch.

2. C — Xylophone
   A xylophone has bars that give different notes, so it can play a tune.

3. A — To make the sound fuller and louder
   The air inside the hollow body makes the sound louder.

4. C — Inside the goal circle
   Shots must be taken from inside the goal circle.

5. D — Wing Attack
   WA is the Wing Attack, who feeds the shooters.

6. C — make a loop
   You make a loop first, pass the end through it and pull tight.

7. A — as you release the ball
   Thumbs turn down as the arms straighten and the ball leaves the hands.

8. C — Three
   Orange, green and purple are the three secondary colours.

9. B — tint
   Adding white makes a tint.

10. D — On the table under the fruit
   A shadow under the object makes it seem to sit on the table.

11. A — Red, yellow and blue
   Primary colours cannot be made by mixing other colours.

12. A — m
   Me is the highest of the three.

13. B — defence of freedom
   The shield and spears represent the defence of freedom.

14. D — green
   Green is at the bottom.

15. D — Gentle jogging and stretching
   Jogging and stretching prepare the body.

16. D — To prepare muscles and avoid injury
   Warm muscles work better and are less likely to be hurt.

17. D — Just behind the start line
   Hands go on the ground just behind the line.

18. A — the blood shed in the struggle for freedom
   Red stands for the blood shed for freedom.

19. D — straight and long like a log
   A straight, tight body rolls smoothly.

20. D — both hands and both feet
   A crab balance rests on two hands and two feet.

21. C — Three to five counts
   Hold the balance for three to five slow counts.

22. B — how loud or soft the music is
   Dynamics are the loud and soft parts.

23. C — everyone sings the same notes at the same time
   Unison means the same notes together.

24. A — how well the subject is lit
   Light is a key element.

25. A — Natural sunlight falling on the subject
   Natural light is best.

26. D — a small light for dark places
   The flash gives extra light.

27. C — Five
   The staff has five lines.

28. A — Left
   The left hand is at the top and the right hand at the bottom.

29. B — long and relaxed with face in the water
   A long relaxed body floats better.

30. C — Mushroom float
   The tucked body with the back at the surface is the mushroom float.

31. C — Not passing urine or spitting in the pool
   Keeping the pool clean matters.

32. A — shout for an adult and throw something that floats
   Do not enter the water; get help and throw a floating object.

33. C — keeping long hair out of the way
   Caps keep hair tidy.

34. D — face up
   Supine is lying on the back.

35. A — balance and coordination
   Moving side to side lightly needs balance.

36. D — Crocodile crawl
   Body held straight on hands and toes.

37. C — by hopping forward with both feet like a hare
   Small quick hops.

38. B — Unity
   The anthem speaks of unity, peace, justice and service.

39. C — Do not touch or write on them
   Care keeps them safe.

40. A — Teamwork and safety
   Teamwork and safety matter.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Remove jewellery, cut long nails, warm up, wear proper shoes, play on flat ground. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each measure.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: When a defender stands close so that the ball must go over their arms.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a defender, 1 mark for going over.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Orange from red and yellow, green from yellow and blue, purple from blue and red.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each secondary colour with its mixture.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the note, decide if it is low, middle or high, and make the hand sign for it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for deciding pitch, 1 mark for hand sign.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk on and off quietly, listen to the leader, do not talk or laugh, clap for others, bow at the end. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold but do not pull; the hawk tags gently; no pushing or tripping; stop at the whistle; take turns. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: A sacred song is a song of worship that praises God. A patriotic song shows love for the country, such as the national anthem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for an example.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Stand tall with a relaxed body. Breathe deeply and sing on the breath. Say the words clearly. Use gestures and facial expressions to show the message and mood. Walk on and off quietly and respect others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five points.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Frog jump, crab walk, elephant walk, snake slither, hare hop, crocodile crawl, giraffe stretch, monkey swing. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say two good things about the work and then give one suggestion for improvement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: To make up a pattern on the spot without writing it first, using an instrument such as a drum or shaker to keep to the beat of a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for making up on the spot, 1 mark for no writing first, 1 mark for using an instrument.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Bending the arms as the ball arrives so as to take the force out of it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bending arms, 1 mark for softening the catch.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: So it does not hit other people, and so the flag can be seen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose four beats. Fill each with a crotchet, a pair of quavers or a rest. Make sure the pattern has variation and ends on a crotchet. Write it with rhythm names and note symbols. Clap it to a steady beat and improve it after feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing beats, using different values, ending on a long note, writing it and performing it.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: A sign for silence for a certain length of time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for silence, 1 mark for length of time.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the outline lightly. Shade the dark parts by pressing harder and the light parts by pressing lightly. Rub the shading with a finger or tissue to blend. Leave the brightest part white.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sing the song and find the beat by tapping. Play the beat on an instrument. Change to a pattern, such as two quick sounds and a long sound. Repeat it and change it at the end of a verse.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step, up to 4.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Squat with hands on the ground. Spring forward with the legs. Land softly on toes and hands with bent knees.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Red, yellow and blue.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for all three, 1 mark for two.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: On your marks, set, go.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for all three, 1 mark for the correct order.
